profile.name: yahoo_finance2_ci_bwrap
profile.scope: A deliberate per-executable and inherited-descendant user namespace exception on a disposable CI VM. It is not an AppArmor workload sandbox and grants no host identity or capabilities.
profile.nestedDesign: Rejected an all-capability-denying child profile and a NET_ADMIN/SETPCAP-only child profile because inherited AppArmor stacking cannot relax the latter for nested Bubblewrap namespace construction.

provisioning.operator: Ordinary non-root operator with zero effective/permitted host capabilities; only confirmed disposable GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 with active AppArmor and default restriction 1.
provisioning.privilegedBoundary: Only fixed, root-owned canonical system utilities and fixed root-controlled destinations run via noninteractive sudo. No repository script or workload runs as root.
provisioning.staging: Fresh atomic /run/yahoo-finance2-ci-apparmor, root-owned 0700; copied regular profile root:root 0600, post-copy digest pinned before parser invocation.
provisioning.parser: Root-owned Ubuntu AppArmor 4 family; --add, /dev/null configuration, --skip-cache. No replacement, broad reload or persistent /etc policy.
provisioning.collisionPolicy: Before any sudo and immediately before add, execute only the canonical plain bwrap with its --args pipe held empty. Two live pidfd/proc snapshots require exact executable identity/argv, unchanged namespaces, ordinary uid/gid, zero effective/permitted/ambient capabilities and literal unconfined label; otherwise refuse. Name filtering is only an additional conservative control. No atomic protection against concurrent privileged policy writers is claimed.
provisioning.failurePolicy: Postflight or loading failure removes only the newly added profile using verified root input and only fixed staging paths. Failed removal preserves the input and keeps the job failed.
provisioning.successLifetime: Profile remains for subsequent tests/Copilot setup session and is discarded with the ephemeral runner.
provisioning.globalPolicy: No sysctl write, AppArmor disable, broad reload, workstation policy change, or weaker retry.

remoteRequiredControls: Before and after exact global user namespace restriction values must match.

Unrelated ordinary-user Python sibling records initial and denial labels/capabilities; fixed same-process ctypes user/network namespace and private NET_ADMIN operations must retain the same EPERM/EACCES denial. No exec-induced capability loss can impersonate the denial.
Existing strict kernel control and full Workers loopback kernel controls run before and after. Distinct private scratch prevents failed before-probe sentinel contamination.

After loading, a nested strict guard and Workers leaf must record the expected profile lineage. The nested leaf repeats actual strict socket, io_uring, read-only and scratch checks; Workers leaf still has all capability sets zero and no_new_privs.
Only observed bwrap permission failures may trigger the scoped remedy. Unrelated preflight failures stop without loading. No fallback or weakened retry is available.

preservedOriginalCandidate.originalReviewResult: Independent Sol and Astra both found accepted P2: loaded names do not identify independently named wildcard executable attachments.

attachmentP2Fix.mechanism: An empty held pipe blocks reviewed Bubblewrap argument parsing before namespace work. Only after two matching live observations is --version plus NUL released. No namespace or workload argument is supplied.
attachmentP2Fix.failureControls: Unknown/denied labels, changed/exited process, executable mismatch, credentials/caps, file capabilities, setuid/setgid, timeout and malformed handshake fail closed. Pinned child is killed/reaped and descriptors close. A signal-denied child receives only empty EOF and exits usage; overall cleanup remains failure.
attachmentP2Fix.execRace: A transient empty procfs argv image is waited on within the deadline, before any label read. All other unexpected observations fail.
attachmentP2Fix.concurrencyContract: Single-job ephemeral trusted host; no concurrent privileged AppArmor or binary writer. Not an atomic kernel policy lock.
